title: Stale taint in buffer spare capacity resurfaces on clean data (research)
claim: Clean overwrites erase ranges only over [start,start+len); ranges in [len,cap) survive. After bytes.Buffer.Read's internal Reset and a shorter clean write, BufferReadFrom from an arbitrary reader republishes the old range over clean bytes via postRanges.
repro_command: GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go test -count=1 -run Test_ReviewStaleCapacityTaint -v ./runtime/taint/ (in a git-archive copy of the research branch; see evidence README.md)

title: Exact provenance bought by pinning every tainted backing array (unbounded memory)
claim: Owner maps hold strong references keyed by address, preventing GC and address reuse; memory grows per distinct tainted value until generation eviction. Documented in README:76-86 and case_104.

title: Generation eviction latches permanent unknown reports on every clean sink
claim: historyDiscarded (and stateSaturated) permanently make every range-free sink value report State=unknown; pinned by lifecycle_test.go:131-179.

title: Every propagation scans all stored ranges under a blocking global lock with no cheap gate
claim: Lookups iterate and allocate over all intervals per generation even for clean values; overlapping writes rebuild and re-sort the full slice under a write Mutex.

title: Request boundary is process-global; concurrent requests evict each other's metadata
claim: StartRequest rotates one global registry list with a single retired slot; concurrent requests drop a live request's generation and taint is never owner-attributed.
